title: The UK and the US are promoting nuclear fusion energy
excerpt: The UK and the US are promoting nuclear fusion energy with deals on supercomputing, artificial intelligence and regulation to accelerate its development.
content:
Both countries are strengthening their cooperation in supercomputing and regulation to accelerate the commercial development of nuclear fusion energy.

Table of Contents
  1. AI accelerates the development of nuclear fusion energy
  2. UK and US strengthen regulatory cooperation
  3. New investments to develop nuclear fusion materials
  4. The fusion industry aims for more than 10,000 jobs by 2030
  5. What's missing to turn nuclear fusion into commercial electricity?

He United Kingdom and United States have taken a new step in their collaboration in nuclear fusion energy with the announcement of two agreements during the World Fusion Policy Summit, held in London on September 14, 2026, both countries seek to accelerate scientific progress, bring this technology closer to commercial application, and create a more favorable environment for investment in the sector.

The alliance brings together expertise in artificial intelligence, supercomputing, and nuclear research, and also envisions greater regulatory coordination, an important aspect for companies working on the development of future fusion power plants.

AI accelerates the development of nuclear fusion energy

One of the agreements brings together the United Kingdom Atomic Energy Authority (UKAEA) and to Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory (PPPL), in the United States, to work together on the development of fusion technologies.

The collaboration will allow both institutions to leverage their experience in artificial intelligence, plasma physics and high-performance computing. These capabilities are fundamental to addressing some of the technical problems that still hinder the construction of commercial fusion plants.

Among its possible applications are the simulation of plasma behavior, the analysis of large volumes of experimental information, and the study of the conditions necessary to maintain fusion reactions in a controlled manner.

Artificial intelligence can also play a significant role by facilitating the interpretation of results and improving research processes. With these tools, scientists hope to accelerate the development of technologies that could one day be used to generate electricity.

UK and US strengthen regulatory cooperation

The second agreement focuses on an equally important aspect for the future of the industry, and that is the regulation of fusion energy.

Through a joint declaration, both governments seek to strengthen regulatory cooperation and facilitate the development of standards that support the growth of this technology.

Having clear rules can offer greater security to companies designing fusion systems and to investors interested in financing new facilities. It is also necessary to move from research laboratories to projects capable of producing electricity on a commercial scale.

Although this collaboration represents progress for the sector, nuclear fusion still has to overcome significant scientific, technical, and economic challenges before becoming a common source of electricity generation.

New investments to develop nuclear fusion materials

During the summit, projects were also announced that seek to expand the UK research and manufacturing capabilities.

One of these projects is a collaboration between the University of Birmingham, the Electric Power Research Institute (EPRI), and several industrial partners, valued at £2.63 million. The work will focus on studying materials that could be used in future applications fusion systems.

The choice of these materials is one of the challenges for the industry, due to the extreme conditions to which the components of the facilities will be exposed, including high temperatures and other effects resulting from nuclear reactions.

Joining this initiative is the Japanese company Kyoto Fusioneering, which announced an investment of up to 3 million pounds sterling in the United Kingdom through the ALBION project.

The funds will be used for the development and testing of materials related to STEP, the British government-backed program working on the design of a prototype nuclear fusion power plant.

With these investments, the country seeks to strengthen its technological and industrial capacity to participate in the future stages of development of this energy source.

The fusion industry aims for more than 10,000 jobs by 2030

The British government’s interest in nuclear fusion is not limited to its potential energy applications, it also considers the economic and employment opportunities that could arise as the industry grows.

According to government forecasts, the development of the sector could support more than 10,000 jobs in the UK by 2030, especially in areas such as physics, engineering, advanced manufacturing and the supply of technological components.

British Energy Minister Michael Shanks highlighted the role that collaboration with the United States can play in translating scientific advances into new industrial and economic opportunities.

For his part, the Minister for the Americas, Chris Elmore, emphasized the importance of leveraging both countries’ capabilities in artificial intelligence, advanced computing, and nuclear fusion. This combination, he explained, will expand opportunities for collaboration between research centers and businesses.

What’s missing to turn nuclear fusion into commercial electricity?

Nuclear fusion is the process by which two light atomic nuclei combine and release large amounts of energy. It is the same phenomenon that allows the Sun to produce light and heat.

Unlike nuclear fission, used in conventional power plants to obtain energy by splitting heavy nuclei, fusion needs to reach extreme temperature and pressure conditions for the reactions to occur.

Its main appeal is the ability to generate electricity without direct carbon dioxide emissions during operation. However, scaling this technology up to commercial levels remains a challenge.

Researchers still need to find solutions to keep the plasma under control, develop materials capable of withstanding the demanding operating conditions, and make the facilities produce electricity efficiently and in an economically viable way.

In this context, the agreements between the United Kingdom and the United States seek to address some of the obstacles separating research from industrial application. Scientific collaboration, the development of standards, and new investments are part of a strategy to pave the way for the first commercial nuclear fusion power plants.
